approach.method_basis: The Parent retains the highest-scoring accepted molecules as breeding parents and fits a fingerprint Gaussian process to every accepted label. It draws a preferred score band, chooses a molecule uniformly inside that band, breeds a fresh pool by graph crossover and mutation, and selects evaluations through correlated posterior draws. Feedback improves the archive, survivor population and posterior, but the parent sampler treats equally ranked eligible parents alike even when their evaluated offspring histories differ.
approach.novelty: Use the actual results of earlier offspring to allocate breeding opportunities within each existing score band. A parent gains credit when an accepted child surpasses the best molecule known before that child's batch; its smoothed historical success fraction determines its within-band sampling weight. This targets productive progress against the same batch incumbent instead of rewarding a child merely for beating a weak generating parent. The completed siblings tested equal core mass and core-diverse survival; this child keeps greedy survival and learns allocation from descendant outcomes.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent n-fc2c108a5253 has complete three-replica posterior-guided graph evolution, with macro mean 0.5443738005952443, but its fixed within-band parent draw ignores whether a parent has produced useful scored descendants. Its 4350 accepted offspring produce 565 strict best-parent beats and 218 sequential incumbent gains. The completed within-core balancing sibling n-69c038cb49ac raises parent-relative beats to 600 but lowers mean generating-parent and offspring scores, with only 216 incumbent gains and a paired final-score mean loss of 0.020256296737091634. The core-round survival sibling n-28dc36ed5be7 broadens breeding but lowers all three replica scores, with paired mean loss 0.029689809698780656; its directly protected weak records never breed. Thus greater diversity or easier parent-relative beats does not by itself identify productive parent allocation. A read-only reconstruction of all fifteen actual Parent logs identifies 286 accepted offspring that strictly beat the incumbent present before their generation batch, giving 6029 parent-outcome credits across 1338 task-local parent identities, including 385 successful parent credits. Of 109919 actual parent draws, 53403 use a parent with at least one earlier scored child but no such incumbent-beating child. On the identical eligible Parent states, the declared smoothed success weights would differ from uniform in 102690 draws, with mean conditional probability total-variation distance 0.2010087676204722. These are retrospective opportunities using only chronologically available labels, not a scored alternative trajectory or an estimate of a causal parent effect.
hypothesis: Weight breeding-parent draws within each inherited score quantile by a smoothed fraction of that parent's earlier accepted offspring that beat their generation batch's pre-feedback incumbent.

finding_summary.headline: Parent-success weighting changed breeding and produced more small gains, but lowered final scores
finding_summary.insights: The historical fraction enriched the intended weight without identifying stronger absolute proposal quality. Its fixed smoothing prior gave untested parents substantial opportunity: their share of actual parent draws rose from 36.91% to 50.50%, while the share with an earlier incumbent-beating offspring fell from 14.51% to 13.39%. Thus much of the observed effect was trying parents with no evaluated offspring history. More progress events against the evolving incumbent did not imply a better search trajectory; their mean size fell from 0.02311 to 0.02068, and the search finished lower. Correctly freezing the reference within a batch removes feedback-order leakage but cannot make different runs' incumbent thresholds equally difficult. These results narrow the useful claim to executable, feedback-sensitive allocation, with negative transfer under this seed panel and budget. Credit is conditional on the posterior selector having chosen an offspring for evaluation, and crossover assigns the same outcome to both parents, so the selected outcome groups cannot establish a causal parent effect. The molecular assessment also found that the modest increase in core coverage retained strained rings, reactive heteroatom variants and oversized repeated assemblies. Parent-outcome credit alone supplied no demonstrated control over those chemical liabilities.
finding_summary.results: Historical credit changed parent selection on the recorded trajectories. Within-band probabilities differed from uniform in 101,614 of 109,053 draws (93.18%), and the selected parent differed from the passive uniform choice using the same random variate in 43,310 draws (39.71%). Selected parents had mean historical weight 0.3649, compared with 0.3037 under uniform selection over those same eligible lists. The accepted archive, score-ranked survival, offspring production and posterior selection retained their prescribed behavior. Among 4,350 scored offspring, strict improvements over the incumbent known before generation increased from 286 to 304, sequential incumbent improvements from 218 to 228, and strict best-parent beats from 565 to 578. These were smaller gains overall: cumulative incumbent improvement across the fifteen task/seed runs fell from 5.0382 to 4.7145. Mean generating-best-parent score fell from 0.4196 to 0.3840, and mean offspring score from 0.3192 to 0.2939. The three-seed final macro mean fell from 0.54437 to 0.52279, a paired mean change of -0.02158; the seed changes were -0.03001, -0.05149 and +0.01676. All five task means fell, with the largest loss on sitagliptin_mpo (-0.05863). The intended +0.002 mean improvement was not achieved.

molecular.headline: Aromatic amides and amines coexist with strained small rings, repeated large assemblies and reactive heteroatom variants
molecular.overall_character: All supplied current and parent trajectories were read; every current task contains 900 molecules and 870 optimizer proposals. The output is strongly aromatic and ring-bearing, with aromatic-token rates from 0.9747 to 0.9874 and ring-closure rates from 0.9874 to 0.9931. Recognizable indole amides, quinoline-linked carbonyl rings and aryl amines coexist with highly constrained small rings, expanded nitrogen-containing diones, reactive nitrogen/oxygen substituents and oversized repeated molecular assemblies. The deco_hop proposal strings have mean length 97.6 and maximum 234, while all tasks also sample very small fragments. Many large products join recognizable fragments without retaining the useful scale or arrangement of the better molecules. All charged-token and stereocentre-token rates are 0.0; the first does not establish neutral solution forms for basic amines, and the second leaves stereogenic saturated frameworks undefined. Diversity is moderate across distinct seed families but locally narrow among the displayed leaders. Several high-scoring products have conventional bonding patterns, yet overall synthetic plausibility remains questionable because strained unsaturated rings, unusual ring connections, N-halogen groups, peroxides and reactive unsaturation persist.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest molecule is a compact bromoindole carboxamide with ethyl, methoxy and N-methyl fluoropyridyl substitution. This is a recognizable, synthetically plausible aromatic amide. Closely scoring relatives replace the indole ring by a benzene-annulated, highly unsaturated small carbon ring, retaining a bromo substituent and an N-methyl pyridyl amide. Other seeds give halogenated enaminone-like aryl compounds or fused aromatic amide frameworks. The low tail includes methane, fluorine, a small cyclic peroxide and a much larger assembly containing repeated aryl/enamide units. Thus the output spans both useful compact aromatic carbonyl chemistry and substantial chemical degeneration.
liabilities: Several near-leading structures contain a benzene-annulated, highly unsaturated small carbon ring with substantial strain and stability concerns.
N-F, N-Cl and alpha-halo carbonyl groups occur in another strong family; these are more reactive than ordinary aryl halogens.
Peroxide fragments, gross molecular duplication and undefined stereochemistry in later fused-ring products remain present.
missing_features: The lowest fragments and repeated large assemblies lack the compact aromatic carbonyl arrangement retained by the leading amides.

The displayed high-scoring series does not systematically preserve ordinary indole-like ring chemistry while varying the useful amide and pyridyl substitution; the best indole shows that a highly strained annulated ring is not necessary for a strong score here.
The N-halo enaminone series lacks a matched set of stable nitrogen substituents preserving the same carbonyl/aromatic arrangement. Equal halogen-swap scores do not establish a chemical requirement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The bromoindole amide scores 0.4387992465191, while the small-ring aromatic amide relative reaches 0.438122145211641. A conventional indole framework therefore already supports the strongest observed score without requiring the more strained alternative. Adding thiol or amino substituents to the small-ring series gives 0.42853301243482195 or 0.42320968985939855. Separate alpha-halo carbonyl/N-halo enamine variants share 0.41048050866648705 despite swapping carbon-bound chlorine for fluorine or N-fluorine for N-chlorine. Those equal values do not demonstrate a need for the reactive bonds. The repeated aryl/enamide assembly scores 6.921499488854122e-25 and tiny fragments score 0.0. Compared with the parent, seed 1 reaches 0.4387992465191 versus 0.4126819838532174 with a sulfur-containing fused framework. Current seed 0 and seed 2 reach 0.41048050866648705 and 0.3918060951569304 versus parental 0.4463521672202675 and 0.4163503402962837.

per_task.generated_character: The displayed leaders connect an O/N-containing aromatic carbonyl heterocycle to a densely cross-connected polycyclic aza-aromatic framework. They carry fluorine, fluoroalkenyl, formate or aldehyde substitution and oxygen-linked terminal alkynes; some relatives replace the other alkyne with ethyl or methoxy. These are rigid and heavily aromatic, with crowded ring connections. Another seed produces smaller aryl-amino carbonyl/thiocarbonyl heterocycles, whereas seed 0 grows very large repeated dione, aryl and acylated nitrogen assemblies. Tiny fragments also remain in the proposal set. The leading fragments are recognizable, but the rigid topology and reactive appendages make the assembled chemistry less straightforward than simple heteroaryl substitution would suggest.
liabilities: Oxygen-linked alkynes, aryl formates, aldehydes and occasional reactive halogen connections complicate chemical stability.
Densely cross-connected aromatic frameworks can demand difficult ring topology even when SMILES parsing succeeds.
Very large repeated dione/acyl/aryl assemblies create a heavy size tail, and extra copies do not consistently improve the recorded score.
missing_features: The smallest fragments lack the connected aromatic and carbonyl/heteroatom organization of the better products.
The large repeated assemblies do not consistently preserve useful chemical scale; the current leaders show that extensive repetition is not necessary for a stronger observed score.

The displayed series incompletely covers ordinary ring topologies and stable substituents that retain the same aromatic polar-group arrangement. The equal-score ethyl/alkyne pair already provides one chemically simpler option.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading aza-aromatic compound scores 0.6175164849513612, compared with 0.6153329352045387 for a closely related structure with carbon at the corresponding aryl position. Replacing the latter's carbon-bound alkyne with ethyl preserves exactly 0.6153329352045387; an alternative more reduced ring arrangement also has that score. Thus the observed scores favor the overall aromatic heterocycle arrangement without demonstrating a need for all unsaturation. Small fragments score 0.5. The largest seed-0 repeated assemblies reach 0.5971495676310452, below the compact leading family, although this cross-family comparison does not isolate size as the only difference. The parent has best scores 0.6004556752278376, 0.6324703199409752 and 0.6083454583246726 across seeds, versus current 0.5971495676310452, 0.6175164849513612 and 0.6115618661257607. Current seed-1 leaders lack the parent's peroxide-chlorine appendage, but still have reactive alkynyl-oxygen and other difficult chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest family contains an aryl-substituted benzene-annulated small carbon ring, phenol, aryl fluorine, a methyl thioether and a saturated diaza ring with an aminomethyl substituent. These provide hydrophobic aromatic surfaces and several potentially basic nitrogen centres. Related molecules replace the aminomethyl connection with imine, enamine or cumulated imine functionality, or add another saturated nitrogen ring. The small carbon ring is strained but has conventional bonds; its multiple stereogenic relationships are unassigned. Low molecules are acid/amide/sulfonamide-rich compounds, small sulfur fragments or very large products combining multiple copies of the stronger frameworks.
liabilities: The benzene-annulated small ring and several substituted saturated centres create strain and stereochemical complexity.
Cumulated imines, cumulated sulfur-containing unsaturation and N-halogenated alternatives introduce reactive functionality.
Aminal-like nitrogen rings, alpha-fluoroamine environments and multiple potentially basic sites need more chemical definition than a neutral unlabelled SMILES provides.
missing_features: The lowest acid/amide/sulfonamide examples lack the accessible aliphatic amine arrangement of the high-scoring family.
The doubled assemblies lose the useful compact size and spacing of the individual aryl/amine framework.

Matched stable alternatives to cumulated imine or thione functionality are incomplete, although the leading aminomethyl molecule already shows that these groups are not essential to a strong observed score.
Relative and absolute configurations across the small carbon ring and substituted diaza ring are unspecified.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aminomethyl-containing leader scores 0.9868145791586695, while its imine relative scores 0.9736699331433097. Several cumulated-imine or thione-containing relatives also score highly, but the strongest displayed molecule does not need those reactive unsaturations. Chlorine and fluorine variants at the saturated diaza ring share 0.973570128548226. Early acid/amide and sulfonamide structures score 0.000719339566735797 and 0.0008839899990958555. Large doubled versions of the aryl/amine framework score only 0.033524275750952556 and 0.03499409918861479. This associates the gradient with a compact aryl/aliphatic-amine arrangement and shows a clear loss when much larger assemblies are formed. Current per-seed maxima are 0.9606175719472576, 0.9250515635604988 and 0.9868145791586695, versus parental 0.9908331648929692, 0.9512348232667347 and 0.9914038363125457. Both generations retain aryl-rich amine chemistry, with different ring frameworks.

per_task.generated_character: The leading compounds connect an ethoxyquinoline-like aromatic group to an expanded nitrogen-rich dicarbonyl ring fused to a small unsaturated nitrogen ring. The latter ranges from an azetene-like connection to still smaller azirine-like alternatives. Carbonyls, NH and N-methyl substituents recur, and some relatives insert an alkylamino linker. Larger alternatives combine additional carbon rings and N/O-containing bridges around the same general aromatic/dicarbonyl motifs. The low tail contains methane, ethane, a hydrocarbon polyene and a small haloacetyl hydroxylamine. The leading compounds are of moderate size but have ring-strain and synthetic-access concerns despite their ordinary amide-like fragments.
liabilities: Small unsaturated nitrogen rings fused to larger carbonyl-containing rings raise strain and stability concerns.
Additional N-N connections, N/O bridges and dense ring closures add chemical complexity in alternative families.
Repeated assemblies and fragment-like products lose the useful organization without supplying a distinct better-performing chemical pattern.
missing_features: The low fragments lack the combined aromatic and dicarbonyl heterocycle arrangement of the stronger molecules.

The leading series lacks enough ordinary, less strained ring connections preserving that arrangement; near-equal scores across ring and linker changes do not establish a need for the smallest unsaturated nitrogen rings.
More elaborate fused alternatives leave possible stereogenic relationships unspecified, while the flatter leading structures still require a feasible constrained ring geometry.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The directly connected ethoxyquinoline/dicarbonyl polycycle scores 0.21529770451127778. Expanding a carbonyl-ring connection gives 0.21407917379021693, while a more contracted small nitrogen-ring arrangement gives 0.21194288404250966. Adding an ethylamino or aminomethyl connection yields 0.21138239979795584 or 0.21008596456279097, and a much larger elaborated polycycle scores 0.21052909287008859. These close values favor retention of the main aromatic/dicarbonyl organization, without showing a need for greater ring complexity or longer linkers. A repeated large final product scores 0.1509909661241802. Tiny fragments score 0.0 and a hydrocarbon polyene scores 0.007693218186208301. Current seed 2 reaches 0.21529770451127778 versus the parent's 0.21037674112349405 with a more expanded quinoline-linked dicarbonyl family; seed 0 and seed 1 reach 0.19245008972987526 and 0.20259185417308956 versus parental 0.22405709718343647 and 0.2133697489012744.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family contains an expanded nitrogen-rich dicarbonyl ring connected through several bonds to a phenolic aromatic system. Fluoromethyl, N-N-linked fluoromethyl or N-methylamino groups and ordinary methyl thioether substitution recur. This is a compact but unusual conjugated polycyclic framework, not a simple isolated dione. Other strong examples contain fluorinated small carbon rings, N-F bonds and N-S-H substituents. The lowest molecules join multiple aromatic dione units into large assemblies. Thus carbonyl and fluorine content are abundant, but their topology, bond type and chemical scale differ sharply across the score range.
liabilities: N-N substituents, direct N-F and N-S-H groups introduce labile or reactive chemistry.
Expanded conjugated nitrogen-rich rings and highly connected aromatic systems require synthetic and geometric scrutiny.
Repeated large dione assemblies and very strained fluorinated carbon-ring alternatives remain in the output.
missing_features: The low repeated assemblies lack the useful compact arrangement of polar groups and fluorinated substituents.
Some weaker close relatives fail to preserve the stronger examples' carbon-linked fluoromethyl organization, substituting direct N-F or additional fluorination instead.

The current displayed leaders do not cover the compact aryl-dione/aminomethyl arrangement of the stronger parent seed-1 molecule; this is a chemical coverage gap, not proof of a uniquely required target motif.
Stereogenic small-ring alternatives have no explicit configurations, while the conjugated expanded-ring leaders require feasible geometry and electronic structure beyond token-level aromaticity.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fluoromethyl-rich phenolic dicarbonyl framework scores 0.5119423040474254; extending its N-N-linked fluorinated side chain gives 0.4904700558333632. A related N-N-linked fluoromethyl structure scores 0.47515676971860416 versus 0.44663453188929914 for its direct N-fluorinated relative. In another displayed pair, changing N-fluoromethyl to N-fluorination gives 0.4257652136908921 rather than 0.49995623590669624; changing it to difluoromethyl gives 0.20047296487227245. Fluorine placement and connection therefore matter more clearly than fluorine abundance. Repeated dione assemblies score as low as 2.9127834142160573e-62. Current seed 2 reaches 0.5119423040474254 versus parental 0.4071395189354175, but seed 0 and seed 1 reach 0.4269183152635783 and 0.352917314371487 versus parental 0.4759777345546235 and 0.5845583988949146. The stronger parent seed-1 family combined a compact aryl dione with carbon-bound aminomethyl and fluorinated substituents, rather than the present expanded ring framework.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The output includes a proposal-string maximum of 234 and mean of 97.6 in its most size-expanded task, alongside fragments such as methane or small halogen-containing species. A compact aryl/amine leader scores 0.9868145791586695, while doubled relatives score 0.033524275750952556 and 0.03499409918861479. Large repeated dione assemblies also occupy the lowest score tail.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful local frameworks are still lost through molecular duplication or degeneration into tiny fragments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve a useful molecular scale and the connected functional-group arrangement when changing structures. Offer meaningful scaffold and linker alternatives without making local variation depend on adding whole copies or deleting most of the framework.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A conventional indole amide scores 0.4387992465191 beside a highly unsaturated small-ring relative at 0.438122145211641. An aminomethyl-bearing structure scores 0.9868145791586695 versus 0.9736699331433097 for its imine relative. An ethyl/alkyne pair has the identical score 0.6153329352045387.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stable, less strained alternatives are not consistently retained despite strong observed examples.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Include matched simplifications that preserve useful aromatic, amine and carbonyl placement while replacing reactive unsaturation or strained ring connections. Distinguish ordinary medicinal bonds from N-halogen, peroxide and cumulated imine/thione functionality.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task has stereocentre-token rate 0.0. Displayed products include substituted benzene-annulated small carbon rings, fluorinated saturated nitrogen rings, small unsaturated nitrogen rings and densely connected polycycles. Some leading flat structures are achiral, but their constrained topology still carries geometric requirements.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stereogenic products and constrained ring systems lack adequate geometric definition.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent feasible stereochemistry where it exists and preserve it through structural edits. Broaden access to ordinary ring sizes and less constrained connections rather than treating successful parsing or aromatic tokens as evidence of feasible three-dimensional chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Several close comparisons distinguish carbon-linked fluoromethyl from direct N-fluorination or additional fluorination, with scores ranging from 0.49995623590669624 to 0.20047296487227245 within a displayed family. Other leading aromatic/dicarbonyl relatives tolerate small linker or ring changes with little score difference, so simple heteroatom or halogen counts do not identify the useful arrangement.
transferable_gaps.gap: Matched placement of polar groups and fluorinated substituents remains incompletely covered.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generate coherent matched series that vary linker length, attachment position, heteroatom identity and fluorine bond type while retaining the remaining framework. Let observed feedback identify which arrangements matter, without assuming that more heteroatoms, fluorines or rings improve a molecule.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
